name: MLOps Interview Prep
subject: mlops
description: CI/CD for ML, model registries, feature stores, monitoring

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a Feature Store in an MLOps pipeline?
options: To store trained model weights
To provide consistent, reusable feature computation for training and serving
To schedule model retraining jobs
To log model predictions in production
questions.explanation: A Feature Store ensures the same feature logic runs at training time and serving time, eliminating training-serving skew.

questions.question: Which metric would you monitor first to detect data drift in a production ML model?
options: GPU utilization
Statistical distribution of input features over time
Number of API requests per minute
Model binary size
questions.explanation: Monitoring input feature distributions (PSI, KL divergence) detects data drift before it degrades model performance.

questions.question: What does a Model Registry primarily store?
options: Raw training datasets
Versioned model artifacts, metadata, and lineage
Feature definitions and transformations
CI/CD pipeline configurations
questions.explanation: A Model Registry tracks versioned model artifacts with metadata like metrics, parameters, and lineage.

questions.question: In a canary deployment for an ML model, what controls the traffic split between old and new model?
options: Feature store routing rules
A load balancer or service mesh weighted routing
The model accuracy threshold
Number of GPUs available
questions.explanation: Traffic splitting in canary release is managed at the infrastructure layer via a service mesh or load balancer.

questions.question: What is the key difference between online and offline feature serving in a Feature Store?
options: Offline serving uses GPUs; online uses CPUs
Online serving provides low-latency lookups for inference; offline provides batch data for training
Offline serving is encrypted; online is not
Online features are computed weekly; offline features are computed in real time
questions.explanation: Online stores (Redis) serve features in milliseconds for inference. Offline stores (S3, BigQuery) serve historical data for training.
